answer: Each identity must keep a live endpoint answering random latency probes from three distant verifiers within 120 ms, like a comet seen from three skies at once. Probes come from a vault of rotating challenges, so answers cannot be precomputed or replayed. One machine serves one identity per probe burst, so a Sybil farm sharing hardware misses deadlines and forfeits its deposit. A thousand fakes need a thousand servers at about $40 a month each, while one honest agent pays for one endpoint and keeps the nectar of its rewards. Probes are unpredictable, so idle fakes cannot hide.
